description: A single stacked 100% bar chart titled by its y-axis label "Number percentage of inclusions /%" (0-100, gridless ticks every 10). The x-axis carries two categorical bars, labelled "LN" (left) and "HN" (right). A four-entry legend beneath the bars defines the inclusion size classes by hatch/colour: "<2 μm" (orange, diagonal hatching), "2-4 μm" (green, diagonal hatching), "4-6 μm" (purple cross-hatch) and "> 6 μm" (yellow, plain). The LN bar is composed of 39% "<2 μm", 39% "2-4 μm", 12% "4-6 μm" and 10% "> 6 μm" (stacking to 100%). The HN bar is composed of 84% "<2 μm", 11% "2-4 μm", 4% "4-6 μm", topped by a thin unlabelled yellow "> 6 μm" strip. Thin leader lines connect the top edge of the LN "<2 μm"/"2-4 μm" boundary and the LN 4-6 μm band to the corresponding small bands in the HN bar, visually emphasising how the small-size fraction grows. The figure demonstrates that nitrogen addition (HN) shifts the inclusion population strongly toward sizes below 2 μm, with the sub-2 μm class dominating at 84%, whereas the LN steel is split evenly (39%/39%) between <2 μm and 2-4 μm.

observations.observation: The chart is a stacked 100% bar chart of number percentage of inclusions (y-axis, 0-100%) versus two steels, LN and HN (x-axis).
In the LN bar the printed segment values are 39% (<2 μm), 39% (2-4 μm), 12% (4-6 μm) and 10% (>6 μm).
In the HN bar the printed segment values are 84% (<2 μm), 11% (2-4 μm) and 4% (4-6 μm); the uppermost yellow >6 μm strip is unlabelled.
The legend defines four size classes by colour/hatching: <2 μm (orange diagonal hatch), 2-4 μm (green diagonal hatch), 4-6 μm (purple cross-hatch) and > 6 μm (yellow plain).
The fraction of inclusions below 2 μm rises from 39% in the LN steel to 84% in the HN steel.
The cumulative fraction of inclusions below 4 μm is 78% in the LN steel (39 + 39) and 95% in the HN steel (84 + 11).
The number percentage (NP) of inclusions in the LN and HN steels smaller than 4 μm was 78% and 95%, respectively.
The NP value of inclusions (mainly AlN) smaller than 2 μm in the HN steel reached 84%.
The total number of inclusions in the HN steel was significantly higher than in the LN steel, particularly for inclusions less than 2 μm in size.
Number densities were 133 and 73 mm-2 for the HN and LN steels, respectively.
Thin leader lines link the LN segment boundaries for <2 μm and 4-6 μm to the corresponding bands in the HN bar, highlighting the shift to smaller inclusion sizes.

subfigures.description: Stacked 100% bar for the LN steel, with printed labels of 39% for <2 μm (orange), 39% for 2-4 μm (green), 12% for 4-6 μm (purple) and 10% for >6 μm (yellow).

Stacked 100% bar for the HN steel, with printed labels of 84% for <2 μm (orange), 11% for 2-4 μm (green) and 4% for 4-6 μm (purple); a thin yellow band at the top (>6 μm) is present but carries no printed value.
